title: Load and prepare heat capacity data
action: Load the raw heat capacity data from the provided silicalite_heat_capacity_data.csv. Separate the data into low-temperature (mean temperature < 40 K) and high-temperature (mean temperature > 20 K) subsets for independent polynomial fitting. Prepare the data arrays for weighted least-squares fitting.
description: Data preparation: reading and partitioning the input data. This step is not scored but is required for subsequent fitting.

title: Fit heat-capacity polynomials
action: Perform weighted least-squares polynomial fitting of the experimental C_p / R data as a function of mean temperature. Fit two separate polynomials: one valid for T < 40 K, another valid for T > 20 K, with a smooth merge near 25.6 K. Output the polynomial coefficients in ascending order (constant term first).
description: Coefficients of the two fitted polynomials that represent the experimental heat capacity data. This artifact is scored by evaluating the polynomials at hidden temperatures against the reference heat capacity values.
output_schema: JSON object with keys 'low_T_poly' (array of floats, coefficients in ascending order for T < 40 K) and 'high_T_poly' (array of floats, coefficients for T > 20 K).

title: Compute thermodynamic functions at 298.15 K
action: Starting from the fitted polynomials and a Debye T³ extrapolation of the heat capacity below 5 K, numerically integrate C_p / T and C_p to obtain the standard molar entropy change Δ₀ᵗ Sₘ° and enthalpy increment Δ₀ᵗ Hₘ° as functions of temperature. Report the values at T = 298.15 K in dimensionless form (C_p / R, Δ₀ᵗ Sₘ° / R, Δ₀ᵗ Hₘ° / (R·K)).
description: Standard molar thermodynamic functions at the reference temperature 298.15 K, computed from the fitted heat-capacity representation and Debye extrapolation.
output_schema: CSV file with header: T, Cp_m_R, DeltaS_R, DeltaH_R_K. Contains one data row with T=298.15 and the computed dimensionless values.
